models.description:
A Machine Learning project that classifies SMS messages
as Spam or Ham using NLP and Naive Bayes classifier
with 97.85% accuracy.

 SMS Spam Detection System
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

OVERVIEW
━━━━━━━━━━━
This notebook presents a complete end-to-end
Machine Learning pipeline to detect whether an
SMS message is Spam or Ham (Not Spam).

The model is trained on the famous UCI SMS Spam
Collection Dataset containing 5,574 real SMS messages
collected from various sources including the Grumbletext
website and NUS SMS Corpus.

The project covers every stage of a real ML pipeline:
Data loading → Cleaning → Preprocessing → Feature
Extraction → Model Training → Evaluation → Prediction.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

 DATASET INFORMATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
→ Name    : UCI SMS Spam Collection Dataset
→ Total   : 5,574 SMS messages
→ Ham     : 4,827 messages (86.6%) — Not Spam
→ Spam    :   747 messages (13.4%) — Spam
→ Format  : CSV (label, message)
→ Source  : UCI Machine Learning Repository

Sample Messages:
  HAM  → "Hey are you coming for lunch today?"
  HAM  → "Meeting postponed see you at 5pm"
  SPAM → "WIN FREE iPhone click here NOW!!!"
  SPAM → "You won 1 lakh rupees claim immediately"

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

 TECH STACK
━━━━━━━━━━━━━
→ Language   : Python 3.x
→ Notebook   : Jupyter Notebook
→ ML Library : Scikit-learn
→ NLP        : NLTK
→ Data       : Pandas, NumPy
→ Visuals    : Matplotlib, Seaborn
→ Platform   : Kaggle

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
 ML PIPELINE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

STEP 1 — DATA LOADING
  → Load spam.csv using Pandas
  → Select label and message columns
  → Encode labels: ham=0, spam=1
  → Check class distribution

STEP 2 — EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS
  → Message length distribution
  → Word count analysis
  → Spam vs Ham comparison
  → Most common spam words
  → Visualizations using Seaborn

STEP 3 — TEXT PREPROCESSING (NLP)
  → Convert to lowercase
  → Remove special characters
  → Remove numbers and punctuation
  → Tokenization (split into words)
  → Remove stopwords (NLTK)
  → Stemming using PorterStemmer
  → Clean text stored in new column

STEP 4 — FEATURE EXTRACTION
  → TF-IDF Vectorization
  → max_features = 3000
  → Converts text to numerical matrix
  → Each message = vector of numbers

STEP 5 — MODEL TRAINING
  → Train/Test Split: 80% / 20%
  → Models trained:
      Naive Bayes (MultinomialNB)
      Logistic Regression
      Support Vector Machine (SVM)
      Random Forest Classifier

STEP 6 — MODEL EVALUATION
  → Accuracy Score
  → Confusion Matrix
  → Precision, Recall, F1 Score
  → Classification Report
  → Model comparison chart

STEP 7 — PREDICTION
  → Predict on new custom messages
  → Real-time spam detection demo

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

 MODEL RESULTS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
┌─────────────────────────
│ Model                   │ Accuracy  │
├─────────────────────────
│ Naive Bayes             │  97.85%   │
│ Support Vector Machine  │  97.40%   
│ Random Forest           │  96.86%   │
│ Logistic Regression     │  95.96%   │
└─────────────────────────

Best Model → Naive Bayes with 97.85% accuracy

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

 ALGORITHMS EXPLAINED
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

NAIVE BAYES:
  → Based on Bayes Theorem
  → Calculates probability of spam
  → Works extremely well with text
  → Fast training and prediction
  → Best choice for spam detection

LOGISTIC REGRESSION:
  → Binary classification (0 or 1)
  → Uses sigmoid activation function
  → Outputs spam probability
  → Good baseline model

SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE:
  → Finds best hyperplane separator
  → Maximizes margin between classes
  → Linear kernel used for text
  → High accuracy on text data

RANDOM FOREST:
  → Ensemble of decision trees
  → Majority voting for prediction
  → Handles overfitting well
  → Robust and reliable

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

 NLP TECHNIQUES USED
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

TF-IDF (Term Frequency — Inverse Document Frequency):
  → TF  = how often word appears in message
  → IDF = how rare word is across all messages
  → TF-IDF = TF × IDF score
  → High score = important word for that message
  → Spam words get high scores in spam messages

Stemming (PorterStemmer):
  → running  → run
  → winning  → win
  → clicking → click
  → Reduces vocabulary size
  → Improves model generalization

Stopword Removal:
  → Removes: is, the, a, an, and, or...
  → Keeps only meaningful words
  → Reduces noise in data

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

 KEY SPAM INDICATORS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

High Spam Words:          High Ham Words:
─────────────────         ─────────────────
FREE, WIN, PRIZE          meeting, today
CLICK, URGENT, NOW        thanks, okay
CLAIM, OFFER, CASH        dinner, lunch
GUARANTEED, WINNER        love, family
MOBILE, AWARDED           project, college
CALL NOW, LIMITED         call, talk, see

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

 CONFUSION MATRIX
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

                  Predicted HAM   Predicted SPAM
Actual HAM    [   True Negative  |  False Positive  ]
Actual SPAM   [  False Negative  |   True Positive  ]

True Negative  → Correctly identified Ham
True Positive  → Correctly identified Spam
False Positive → Ham wrongly classified as Spam
False Negative → Spam wrongly classified as Ham

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
